The Taifa of Denia page says the army 'settled a military camp in the north of the island for one year' (1015-1016) and names no judicate. Reading 'the north' as Gallura and Logudoro, the reduced shape holds for 1015-1016 only; the full shape returns in 1017. The page describes a camp, not a conquest of the whole judicate, so the cut-out is Cliopatria's stand-in.
4,598 km2: north-east Sardinia round Olbia, ten curatoriae. Applies from 1017 (see the 1015 verdict). No infobox area.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Gallura shape after 1209. In 1258 the Judicate of Cagliari was divided: it.wikipedia (Giudicato di Cagliari) gives Gallura 'la parte di nord-orientale (Ogliastra, Sarrabus)', Arborea 'la parte zona centro-settentrionale', the Della Gherardesca 'la regione occidentale del Sulcis-Iglesiente' and Pisa Castel di Castro 'fino al 1326'; the English Cagliari page says only 'three parts' for the Della Gherardesca, Arborea and Gallura. The it.wikipedia Gallura page lists more for Gallura ('parte delle Barbagie, l'Ogliastra, Gippi e il Sarrabus'); the Barbagie part and Gippi are not drawn because the Cagliari page names only Ogliastra and the Sarrabus and no page opened locates the others. The addition is Cliopatria's 1187 Cagliari shape intersected with the Natural Earth province Ogliastra and a 25 km radius round Muravera for the Sarrabus (six comuni listed on it.wikipedia Sarrabus; the radius is a stand-in and its centre is the dossier's, not a page's). Size in gazetteer cells: 14 for the 1206 outline (Cliopatria: 4,598 km2) and 13 added, about 3,300 km2, a little under two fifths of Cagliari's 33 cells. The page gives no infobox area to compare. Soft.

ledger.note: 1207: Elena marries the Pisan Lamberto Visconti, who repulses the Cagliari invasion. In 1207 she married the Pisan Lamberto Visconti, who repulsed the invasion (Gallura page). The repulse is dated by the marriage year.

1207: the Visconti of Pisa become the judges of Gallura. Lamberto Visconti ruled until his death in 1225; the Visconti line began in 1207 and ended with Nino's deposition in 1287 (History of Sardinia page: through marriage Gallura passed to the Visconti family in 1207). Same state and land; the dynasty changes from the Lacon line.

ledger.note: 1258: Gallura receives the north-east third of the Judicate of Cagliari when Pisa and the other judicates divide it. it.wikipedia (Giudicato di Cagliari): Gallura received 'la parte di nord-orientale (Ogliastra, Sarrabus)'; the English Cagliari page: the territory was 'partitioned in three parts', 'assigned to the Della Gherardesca family, Arborea and Gallura'. A second page, it.wikipedia Giudicato di Gallura, has Gallura gaining 'con la divisione di quello di Cagliari nel 1258 parte delle Barbagie, l'Ogliastra, Gippi e il Sarrabus'; the extra pieces are not drawn (see the 1258 keyframe). The Sarrabus is the six comuni of it.wikipedia Sarrabus, a curatoria of Cagliari. Neither page gives a month; the region is the dossier's reading of the two names.

ledger.note: 1287: Nino Visconti is deposed and Gallura passes to Pisa. Nino Visconti was deposed from Gallura in 1287, ending Visconti rule that began in 1207; Pisa held Gallura until the Aragonese conquest of 1323-1324 (Gallura page). The History of Sardinia page dates the removal of 'the last judge, Nino Visconti' to 1288 and the Gallura infobox says 'Disestablished: 1296'; the article's own text is followed. The land handed over is the 1258 outline, including the third of Cagliari gained in 1258 (Pisa annexed Gallura, Gallura page). The it.wikipedia Gallura page dates Nino Visconti's death to 1296 and has Pisa governing Gallura directly through a vicar 'dal 1300', so Pisa's hold is firm by 1300 at the latest; the English text's 1287 is kept.

wars.name: Dénia invasion of Sardinia

zones.text: the north of the island, where the Dénia army 'settled a military camp ... for one year' (Taifa of Dénia page); drawn as the part Cliopatria cuts from Gallura in 1015-1017

wars.outcome: The Dénia army held a camp in the north of Sardinia for one year; the fleets of Pisa and Genoa reconquered the island; Mujahid's heir Ali Iqbal al-Dawla was captured and ransomed only in 1032.
wars.note: The page names no judicate and no date for the reconquest; the Mujahid al-Amiri page puts the occupied land in the south.

wars.name: Cagliari's invasion of Gallura
wars.outcome: William I of Cagliari invaded in 1206 and was repulsed by Lamberto Visconti, who married the heiress Elena in 1207.

wars.name: Genoese and Torres attack on Gallura
wars.outcome: In 1211 Comita III of Torres made a treaty with Genoa to conquer the island, Gallura first; Pisa struck back in 1212 after Gallura was attacked; Pope Honorius III forced a settlement on 1 December 1217.
wars.note: No ground taken or held is recorded, so no zone and no contest event are written.

notes: FOUNDING: Cliopatria starts the row in 866; the page says Established: 11th century and little is known from the mid-9th to early 11th century, with a single archontate over the whole island by the 9th century. The dossier keeps 866 at confidence 1 as Cliopatria's year; a gap-filler may prefer c.1020 (Manfred, infobox) or c.1050 (the text). END: Cliopatria ends 1209; the page runs the judicate to 1287 (text), 1288 (History of Sardinia) or 1296 (infobox 'Disestablished'); 1287 is used. Pisa held Gallura to 1323-24 (Gallura and Pisa pages) and should carry a matching gain in 1287 (republic-of-pisa, eu-13). DENIA: the Taifa of Denia dossier hatches the 193 km2 remnant of Gallura as the occupied land; the camp was in 'the north of the island', so the dossier here hatches the part Cliopatria cuts out. Cagliari's dossier and this one disagree with the Denia page on where the army sat (south on the Mujahid page, north on the Denia page). PERSONAL UNIONS (no territory event written, rule 4): the Gallura page says of Logudoro that in 1236 it was acquired through marriage to Adelasia; the Adelasia page has her acclaimed judge of Logudoro in her own right in 1236, married to Ubaldo II of Gallura in 1219 and then to Enzo in 1238, and holding the titular judgeship of Gallura 1238-1257 while the Gallura page has Giovanni Visconti succeeding Ubaldo (d. 1238); the pages do not agree on who ruled Gallura 1238-1257. PISAN HOMAGE: Comita I paid homage to the archbishop of Pisa around 1130 and again at Ardara on 26 June 1132; religious supremacy, no event. The page's statement that around 1100 the Pisans were expelled by the Thori dynasty is too vague to date a territorial change. RULERS: the infobox lists Manfred 1020-1040, Elena 1200-1225 and Nino Visconti 1276-1296, which conflict with the text (Lamberto to 1225, Nino deposed 1287); no ruler strip is written. COORDINATES of Olbia are the gazetteer's. Budget: five pages. No gazetteer name is needed. REPAIR 2026-10-25: (1) 1258 GAIN added from the Cagliari partition: it.wikipedia Giudicato di Cagliari gives Gallura 'la parte di nord-orientale (Ogliastra, Sarrabus)'; ledger gain 1258 (confidence 2), keyframe 1210 now ends 1257 and keyframe 1258 (1258-1287) is the 1206 outline plus the Cagliari third; the 1287 dissolve and Pisa's successor land use the enlarged outline. The it.wikipedia Gallura page adds 'parte delle Barbagie' and 'Gippi', which the Cagliari page does not; these two are not drawn and need a page that locates them. The Sarrabus is a 25 km radius round Muravera (gazetteer has neither name; gazetteer agent: add a region Sarrabus = Burcei, Castiadas, Muravera, San Vito, Villaputzu, Villasimius). Gallura's part in the 1258 siege of Santa Igia (Pisa 'and the other judicates', Cagliari page) is not dated or located on any page and no contest event is written. Cagliari's own dossier still lists the 1258 successor lands as the whole shape; the parts are on the it.wikipedia page. (2) FOUNDING: it.wikipedia Giudicato di Gallura was opened for a founding date and has none in its text (the infobox, Established: 11th century, is on the English page); 866 stays at confidence 1. (3) END: it.wikipedia puts Nino Visconti's death at 1296 and direct Pisan rule at 1300; 1287 (English text, spot-checked by the reviewer) is kept. Pages: eight in all, three over the five-page budget at the reviewer's request.
